text: Soilborne diseases: (1) Fusarium wilt — V-shaped yellowing spreading up from lower leaves, whole plant eventually wilts and dies; no cure, only preventive fungicides (Carbendazim, Carboxin, Copper Oxycloride). (2) Bacterial wilt — sudden wilting with milky bacterial ooze visible when a cut stem is squeezed and the two cut ends pulled apart slowly, forming sticky threads; no chemical cure exists. (3) Root-knot nematode — stunted, pale, wilting plants with swollen/galled roots; no chemical cure, only prevention via crop rotation and reducing plastic-mulch reuse from infested beds. Viral: Cucumber Mosaic Virus — mottled dark/light green leaves curling downward, stunted growth, no yield; no cure, only prevention via resistant varieties and controlling aphid/whitefly vectors that transmit it.
